name: Ranger Herbal Savant
body:
Herbal savants have a stronger connection to flora than most rangers. They have a knack for taking advantage of a medicinal plant’s curative power, while resisting any toxic effects.

An herbal savant has the following class features.

Skilled Botanist (Ex)

At 1st level, an herbal savant must select plant as his favored enemy. Furthermore, an herbal savant gains a +2 competence bonus on Fortitude saving throws made against all plant poisons, and is always treated as though he has a number of skill ranks equal to his herbal savant level in Knowledge (nature) when making a skill check regarding plants and plant creatures. Finally, an herbal savant gains woodland stride at 1st level rather than 7th level.

This alters favored enemy and woodland stride, and replaces wild empathy.

Botanical Medic (Su)

An herbal savant combines the botanical gifts of nature with his own magical essence to create curative tonics to restore his health during the course of the day. Only the herbal savant can gain the curative benefit of his tonics. At 2nd level, an herbal savant can create a number of curative tonics equal to 1 + his Wisdom modifier. At 6th level, and every four levels thereafter, an herbal savant can create one extra tonic. An herbal savant’s tonic cures a number of hit points equal to 1/2 his herbal savant level + 1d6 points of damage. For every three levels beyond 2nd, the damage the tonic cures increases by +1d6, to a maximum of +7d6 at 20th level.

Each morning, after 8 hours of rest, an herbal savant must spend 10 minutes creating his curative tonics. A tonic, once created, remains potent for 1 day before becoming inert, so an herbal savant must prepare his curative tonics every day. Imbibing a curative tonic is treated in the same manner as drinking a potion with regards to the action type required and whether it provokes an attack of opportunity.

This replaces all combat style feats, quarry, and improved quarry.

Green-Bond (Ex and Sp)

At 4th level, an herbal savant gains the plant domain or any of the plant subdomains of his choice. He can even select two subdomains as long as when the two subdomains are combined, they replace different domain powers. For example, an herbal savant could select both the decay and growth subdomains because the decay subdomain replaces the bramble armor power and the growth subdomain replaces the wooden fist power.

In addition to gaining the domain powers at the specified levels, the herbal savant adds the domain spells to his ranger spell list as soon as he is capable of casting spells of the appropriate level. (He never gets the spells of 5th level and above.) Finally, the herbal savant adds the following spells to his ranger spell list: goodberry at 4th level, plant shape l at 7th level, plant shape ll at 10th level, and plant shape lll at 13th level.

This replaces hunter’s bond.
